nodes.label: Vevit account as OIDC provider: contract with VeVit Office
Vevit account as OIDC provider
nodes.rationale: vevit.cz/account acts as the single OIDC issuer for VeVit Office (online and cloud) so paired devices sign in with the same Vevit identity; the source of truth is docs/OIDC-SPEC.md in the vevit-office repo and this monorepo keeps an unchanged copy.

nodes.label: Authorization code flow (PKCE S256)
nodes.rationale: nonce and PKCE S256 are mandatory; client/redirect errors are answered on the page (400) and never redirected; the code is 256 random bits, valid 60 s, single use, stored only as SHA-256; a failed verifier burns the code.

nodes.label: RFC 8628 device flow
nodes.rationale: Device endpoints serve only vevit-office-device; the code-flow client vevit-office is refused there; an approved device code is consumed by one atomic conditional update; the device-flow ID token is bound to the client (aud = vevit-office-device), not to a server, because a desktop sign-in is not tied to a paired server.

nodes.label: ES256 key rotation via JWKS
nodes.rationale: ID tokens live 5 minutes and Office caches the JWKS for an hour, so rotation publishes both keys and swaps in three steps at least an hour apart; keys come only from the environment and kid is derived from the public key so no extra variable can drift.

nodes.label: ID token claims contract (ES256, kid)
nodes.rationale: sub is public.users.id, stable and never reused; aud is the client_id (code-flow tokens carry aud = vevit-office plus the exact device redirect URI); email_verified is true only when users.email_verified_at is set so Office cannot admit anybody by an unverified address.

nodes.label: Device link and pairing API (/link/start, /link/poll, /link/confirm)
nodes.rationale: Codes, device codes, user codes, poll tokens and device tokens are stored as SHA-256 only; the one recoverable secret (the device token between confirmed and collected, at most 10 minutes) is AES-256-GCM sealed with OFFICE_LINK_SEAL_KEY and wiped on collection; device names are never reused after unlinking and are limited to 10 per account.

nodes.label: ACME DNS-01 TXT record API (/dns/acme)
nodes.rationale: A device may only write its own _acme-challenge.<name>.office.vevit.cz record with a 43-character base64url value, authenticated by its bearer device token, backing DNS-01 certificates for the relay.

nodes.label: Fail-closed atomic rate limiting (office_rate_limits)
nodes.rationale: A new atomic SQL counter (office_rate_consume / office_rate_limits) is used instead of login_attempts whose column types are not in the repository; any limiter outage answers 503 so the system fails closed.

nodes.label: Office audit log (HMAC of IP, no secrets)
nodes.rationale: The audit log stores an HMAC of the IP (OFFICE_AUDIT_IP_SECRET), never the address and never secrets or TXT values; audit write failures are logged but never fail the request.

nodes.label: Third-party device consent screen
nodes.rationale: Consent applies only to somebody else's device; the owner and the first-party Cloud never see it; consents are per user and device and die with the device.

nodes.label: Stripe inert webhook and office_plans billing
nodes.rationale: Stripe is wired as an inert webhook (signature, 5-minute tolerance, price-to-plan map); plans are rows in office_plans that an administrator edits by hand until real billing exists; unconfigured answers 503.

nodes.label: E-mail verification flow
nodes.rationale: email_verified is false until users.email_verified_at is set because registration here does not verify addresses; the one-time link holds a 256-bit token valid 24 hours, stored as SHA-256 only, and a page button (not the GET) spends it so mail scanners cannot; changing users.email un-verifies via a database trigger (migration 027) so every code path including legacy PHP is covered; resends are limited to 1/min and 3/hour per person.

nodes.label: OfficeStore interface (Supabase in production, memory in tests)
nodes.rationale: Handlers are plain (deps, Request) => Response functions over an OfficeStore interface so every endpoint is tested with node --test without a Next.js runtime or a database.

nodes.label: DnsAdapter abstraction
nodes.rationale: The DNS provider sits behind DnsAdapter; until a real adapter exists the endpoints answer 503, and the mock (OFFICE_DNS_PROVIDER=mock, previews only) cannot be enabled by accident in production because the variable is unset there.

nodes.label: vevit-office public OIDC client (code flow)
nodes.rationale: Public PKCE S256 client with no secret; its redirect URI is validated against the registered shape and the live device table on every request, and again at the token endpoint against the URI stored with the code.

nodes.label: vevit-office-device client (device flow)
nodes.rationale: Serves the RFC 8628 device endpoints; the vevit-office repo needs a separate device_client_id setting so the Office server sends client_id=vevit-office-device there, since the provider refuses vevit-office on those endpoints.

nodes.label: GET /subscription endpoint
nodes.rationale: Returns name in addition to the four documented fields because vevit-relay registers devices by it; an unlinked device gets 401 at once.

nodes.label: office_purge_expired() daily pg_cron purge
nodes.rationale: Runs daily from pg_cron inside Supabase (no public endpoint, no CRON_SECRET); Vercel Cron was rejected because it would need both.

nodes.label: Office SQL migrations 026-028
nodes.rationale: 026_office_oidc.sql adds users.email_verified_at, 11 tables with RLS, 3 functions and 2 default plans; 027_office_email_verification.sql adds verification tokens, the trigger on users.email and a wider purge; 028_office_purge_cron.sql schedules the daily purge.
